newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks' capital adequacy ratios at end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks' capital adequacy ratios at end-Sept.

text.p: Japan's 20 biggest banks said on Monday that their preliminary international capital adequacy ratios at the end of today, the last day of the the first half of the 1996/97 business year, were as follows.
Under rules set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally must have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
Unlike many other countries, Japan allows banks to include unrealised profits on shareholdings as part of their capital.
The 225-share Nikkei average finished at 21,556.40 on Monday, the last business day before banks close their books for the first half of the 1996/97 business year.
The index stood at 21,406.85 on March 29, 1996, the last trading day of the 1995/96 fiscal year.

Banking industry sources said the 20 banks managed to keep their capital/asset ratios above eight percent at the end of March because they realised a huge amount of hidden profits on sales of shareholdings to cover the problem loan write-offs.
The full names of the long-term credit banks are:
Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.

The commercial banks are: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd, Sakura Bank Ltd, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, Fuji Bank Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd, Asahi Bank Ltd, Daiwa Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd.

The trust banks are: Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp, Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd and Nippon Trust Bank Ltd.
